extracted.intended_audience: parties to ITC section 337 investigations (complainants/respondents), patent attorneys, and other stakeholders in trade remedy proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Notice of the U.S. International Trade Commission's determination to grant a joint motion to terminate a remand investigation based on settlement, describing procedural history and the legal/administrative standards the Commission applied. Useful for practitioners preparing or evaluating motions to terminate, settlement filings, or remand proceedings under section 337 and 19 CFR part 210.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with Commission Rule 210.21(b)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission determined that the motion complies with the requirements of Commission Rule 210.21(b)(1) (19 CFR 210.21(b)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The motion included exhibits (confidential and public versions of the settlement agreement). The parties' motion also included a statement that "there are no other agreements, written or oral, express or implied between Lashify and Hollyren concerning the subject matter of this Investigation." The motion served as the parties' response to the Commission's July 30, 2025 Notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint motion to terminate based on settlement and consent arbitration award (19 CFR 210.21(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A joint motion to terminate the investigation may be filed based on the moving parties' settlement agreement and consent arbitration award under 19 CFR 210.21(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The motion should attach the settlement agreement (public and confidential versions as appropriate) and identify any consent arbitration award relied upon. Parties must make clear that the settlement addresses the subject matter of the investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of extraordinary circumstances preventing termination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission must find that there are no extraordinary circumstances that would prevent the requested termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If extraordinary circumstances exist, the Commission may deny termination even if procedural filing requirements are met. The notice states the Commission made an explicit finding that no such extraordinary circumstances exist for this motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting termination must not be contrary to the public interest (Commission Rule 210.50(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission must determine that granting the motion would not be contrary to the public interest pursuant to Commission Rule 210.50(b)(2) (19 CFR 210.50(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission considered the public interest standard and found that granting the joint motion would not be contrary to the public interest in this matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfaction of domestic industry requirement — technical prong
rubrics_metrics.description: A complainant must satisfy the technical prong of the domestic industry requirement for asserted patents; failure to satisfy the technical prong can lead to termination of a patent from the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice records prior Commission findings that Lashify failed to satisfy the technical prong for certain patents (e.g., the '388 and the '984 patent as to certain claims), which earlier resulted in termination of those patents or claims from the investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfaction of domestic industry requirement — economic prong (significant employment of labor or capital)
rubrics_metrics.description: To satisfy the economic prong of the domestic industry requirement, a complainant must demonstrate substantial domestic economic investment, often framed as "significant employment of labor or capital."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Federal Circuit vacated the Commission's determination as to the economic prong for the Asserted Patents and remanded the matter to determine whether there is "significant employment of labor or capital" with respect to the two design patents (D'416 and D'664). A proper economic-prong showing is therefore a critical element on remand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial withdrawal of complaint can terminate specific claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A complainant's partial withdrawal of the complaint can result in termination of certain claims from the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission previously terminated various claims of the asserted patents based on Lashify's partial withdrawal of the complaint (the notice cites several Order Nos accomplishing such terminations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of a respondent based on Consent Order
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may be terminated from the investigation by entry into a Consent Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice cites the termination of Rachael Gleason d/b/a Avant Garde Beauty Company from the investigation based on a Consent Order (Order No. 28).

rubrics_metrics.name: Role and weight of OUII responses
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Unfair Import Investigations (OUII) participates as a party and may file responses addressing what proceedings, if any, should occur on remand; OUII support can affect the Commission's decision to proceed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter OUII filed a response stating that the motion, if granted, would obviate the need for further proceedings and also filed a separate response in support of the motion. OUII's position was noted by the Commission when granting the motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing and public access requirements — EDIS and non-confidential documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of non-confidential documents filed in connection with the investigation may be viewed on the Commission's electronic docket (EDIS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice provides the EDIS URL (https://edis.usitc.gov) and an EDIS help email (EDIS3Help@usitc.gov). Parties should ensure appropriate public/non-confidential versions of filings are submitted for docketing and public access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency authority basis: section 337 and Part 210
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority for Commission determinations is contained in section 337 of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended (19 U.S.C. 1337), and in Part 210 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure (19 CFR part 210).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions, terminations, and other procedural actions are reviewed and decided pursuant to these statutory and regulatory authorities; references to these authorities should be included in filings and notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural history and appeal/remand process impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior Commission orders, Federal Circuit appeals, vacaturs, and remands shape what must be considered or re-litigated on remand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice summarizes prior Commission terminations, the Commission's 2022 final determination, Lashify's appeal, the Federal Circuit's March 5, 2025 decision vacating the economic-prong determination and remanding certain issues, the denial of rehearing, and the issuance of the court mandate—demonstrating that appellate outcomes and remand scope materially affect Commission proceedings and the content of termination motions.
